## The pillars of the Web

:::: {.fragment .fade-in}

### Abstraction
A **general, extensible model** applicable to *many concrete domains*.

- ***Messages*** \ ➝ \ interoperable ***information***
- ***Objects*** \ ➝ \ interoperable ***interaction***
- ***Certificates*** \ ➝ \ interoperable ***authentication***
- ***Tokens*** \ ➝ \ interoperable ***authorization***

- ***Messages*** \ ➝ \ interoperable ***exchange***

### Neutrality
**Open** to participation **without discrimination**.

- No single authority
- No licensing costs
- No minimum quality

# European Digital Identity

## Regulations

::: {.columns}
:::: {.column .fragment .fade-in}

### Legal structure

  - **EIDAS** (2014)
    - Trust services
    - Levels of assurance
    - Trusted lists for qualification

  - **EBSI** (2018)
    - Blockchain services

  - **ESSIF** (2019)
    - Self-Sovereign Identity (SSI)

  - [**EUDI** (2024)]{.mark}
    - [Digital identity wallet]{.mark}
    - [Trusted lists for participation]{.mark}

::::
:::: {.column .fragment .fade-in}

### Technical structure (EUDI)

  - Implementing regulations

  - **Architecture & Reference Framework** (ARF)

    - **ETSI** (infrastructure)
    - **ENISA** (cryptography)
    - [**OpenID** (protocol)]{.mark}
      - [Verifiable Credential Issuance (OpenID4VCI)]{.mark}
      - [Verifiable Presentations (OpenID4VP)]{.mark}
    - **ISO**, **IETF**, **W3C** (credentials)

::::
:::

## Neutrality: institutionalized 'trust'

> #### EUDI as advertised (Q&A, recitals ...)
> ##### *Citizens will be in **full control** over **which data** they share with **which parties**.*[\*]{.fragment .fade-in fragment-index=1}

:::: {.fragment .fade-in fragment-index=1}
\* [Fineprint]{.underline}:

  - issuers, wallets, and verifying parties must be included in a **trusted list**,
  - based on *[**legal**, **financial**, and **operational** criteria]{.remark-nope} (e.g., liability, continuity, reporting ...)*,
  - approved by [***government institutions***]{.remark-nope}.
    <br/><br/>
::::

. . .

### Impact reports

Participation in the EU Digital Identity space dependent on [**economical** and **political** incentives]{.remark-nope}, <br/> putting it at risk for [**commercial** and **criminal** exploitation]{.remark-nope}.

[(ISOC, CEPIS, CA/B, EFF)]{.aside style="font-size:0.8em;color:darkgrey;"}

## Abstraction: reinventing 'identity'

> #### OpenID's "new trust model"
> ##### *A [paradigm shift]{.underline} towards user-centricity, increasing **portability**, **privacy**, and **control***

::::: {.fragment .fade-in fragment-index=1}
- ***Portability***
  - [Bring Your Own Identity]{}
    [[... like OpenID Connect]{.remark-oidc}]{.fragment .fade-in fragment-index=7}
  - [Offline/asynchronous availability]{-index=8}
    [[... like OpenID Connect]{.remark-oidc}]{.fragment .fade-in fragment-index=7}
  - [No pre-established verifier--issuer relations]{.fragment .semi-fade-out fragment-index=5}
    [... apart from *trust* relations]{.fragment .fade-in-then-semi-out .remark-nope fragment-index=4}
:::::

::::: {.fragment .fade-in fragment-index=2}
- ***Privacy***
  - [Presentation without issuer]{}
    [[... like OpenID Connect]{.remark-oidc}]{.fragment .fade-in fragment-index=7}
  - [Verification without issuer]{.fragment .semi-fade-out fragment-index=6}
    [... impossible for PKI-based proofs]{.fragment .fade-in-then-semi-out .remark-nope fragment-index=5}
:::::

::::: {.fragment .fade-in fragment-index=3}
- ***Control***
  - [Informed consent]{}
    [[... like OpenID Connect]{.remark-oidc}]{.fragment .fade-in fragment-index=7}
  - [Selective disclosure]{.fragment .semi-fade-out fragment-index=7}
    [... not needed without wallets]{.fragment .fade-in-then-semi-out .remark-nope fragment-index=6}
:::::

# Back to the drawing board

## A self-sovereignty based on mutual trust

**The standard we have**: <br/>
A 'local cache' to manage [**consent**]{.red} for the [access]{.green} to [(signed) personal info]{.blue} by [approved parties]{.orange}.

. . .

**The standard we need**: <br/>
A 'remote key' to manage [**delegated control**]{.red .underline} *for [any interaction]{.green} with [any (authentic) service]{.blue} by [any party]{.orange}*.

. . .

<br/>

### Delegation of control

*Sharing decision-making power with another person*

- **demonstrates trust** of the *delegator* in the *delegate*;
- **builds trust** of the *delegate* in the *delegator*.

## Too complicated? A practical approach ...

. . .

1. **Description**
   - Technical APIs [(e.g., OpenAPI)]{.ex}
   - Legal/industrial DSLs [(e.g., Data Privacy Vocabulary)]{.ex}

. . .

2. **Authentication**
   - Signatures, PKI, ledgers [(e.g., EBSI)]{.ex}
   - Certificates, credentials [(e.g., VC)]{.ex}
   - Federations [(e.g., OpenID Federation, informative Trusted Lists)]{.ex}

. . .

3. **Control**
   - Policy evaluation [(e.g., Open Digital Rights Language, Wallet Access Control Engine)]{.ex}
   - Policy enforcement [(e.g., OAuth 2.1; Privacy Processing Receipts)]{.ex}
   - Policy management [(e.g., User-Managed Access, Grant Negotiation & Authorization Protocol, Authorization for Data Spaces)]{.ex}

. . .

4. **Delegation**
   - Federation
   - Attenuation [(e.g., Biscuits)]{.ex}
